'''Robert Alan Huggins''' is professor emeritus at the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at the [[Stanford University School of Engineering|School of Engineering]] at [[Stanford University]]<ref name="Emeritus">{{cite web |title=Robert Huggins Professor of Materials Science and Engineering, Emeritus |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/robert-huggins |website=Stanford University School of Engineering |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref> and Honorary Professor at the [[University of Kiel]] and the [[University of Ulm]]. He was previously Chief Scientist at the Center for Solar Energy and Hydrogen Research in Ulm.
The [[International Society for Solid State Ionics]] (ISSI) held a  symposium in his honor in 2009, in recognition of his work on fundamental properties and behavior of materials, [[Solid state ionics|solid state ionic]] probing techniques, catalytic behavior at gas–solid interfaces, and the development of electrodes for [[Lithium-ion battery|Lithium Ion batteries]].<ref name="Gür"/>

==Education ==
Robert Alan Huggins is the son of chemist [[Maurice Loyal Huggins]], known for the [[Huggins equation]] and the [[Flory–Huggins theory]].<ref name="Gür"/>

Robert Huggins earned his BA in [[Physics]] from [[Amherst College]], and went on to obtain an MS and Sc.D. in [[Metallurgy]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where he also served as an instructor.<ref name="ECS"/>

==Career ==
Huggins joined the Stanford faculty in 1954. He established Stanford's Department of Materials Science and Engineering in 1959 and its [[Materials Research Science and Engineering Centers|Center for Materials Research]] program in 1961.<ref name="Leslie">{{cite book |last1=Leslie |first1=Stuart W. |title=The Cold War and American science: the military-industrial-academic complex at MIT and Stanford |date=1993 |publisher=Columbia University Press |location=New York |isbn=978-0-231-07959-4 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6IchaV00dBkC&pg=PA212 |access-date=29 September 2021|pages=212–233}}</ref><ref name="Gür"/> He became a full professor in 1962.<ref name="ECS">{{cite web |title=Robert Huggins |url=https://www.electrochem.org/huggins |website=The Electrochemical Society |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref>  
Huggins also served as Director of Materials Sciences  at the [[Advanced Research Projects Agency]] (ARPA) in Washington, D.C. from 1968 to 1970.<ref name="Gür"/>

Huggins spent a [[sabbatical]] in 1965 and 1966 working with [[Carl Wagner]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Biophysical Chemistry]] in [[Göttingen]], Germany,<ref name="Gür" /> an experience he later described as pivotal for his later work on lithium-ion batteries.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Fletcher|first=Seth|title=Bottled Lightning: Superbatteries, Electric Cars, and the New Lithium Economy|publisher=Macmillan|year=2011}}</ref> He was one of the founders of the [[Materials Research Society]] in 1973. In 1987 he co-founded the [[International Society for Solid State Ionics]] (ISSI), serving as its first President from 1987 to 1989.<ref name="Gür">{{cite journal |last1=Gür |first1=Turgut M. |title=Solid state ionic tools for catalysis and materials research: In honor of Robert A. Huggins |journal=Solid State Ionics |date=June 2011 |volume=192 |issue=1 |pages=645–652 |doi=10.1016/j.ssi.2009.12.013 |doi-access= }}</ref>
Huggins was the founding [[editor-in-chief|editor]] of the ''[[Annual Review of Materials Science]]'' from 1971 to 1993<ref name="Kaufmann">{{cite journal |last1=Kaufmann |first1=Elton N. |title=Preface |journal=Annual Review of Materials Science |date=August 1994 |volume=24 |issue=1 |article-number=annurev.mr.24.072806.100001 |doi=10.1146/annurev.mr.24.072806.100001 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
and the editor of the journals ''[[Solid State Ionics]]'' and ''Materials Research Bulletin''.<ref name="SSI">{{cite journal |last1=Huggins |first1=Robert A. |title=Solid State Ionics |journal=MRS Bulletin |date=September 1989 |volume=14 |issue=9 |pages=18–21 |doi=10.1557/S0883769400061698 |bibcode=1989MRSBu..14...18H |s2cid=97482401 }}</ref>

As of October 1991, Huggins became the Chief Scientist of the Energy Storage and Conversion Division at the [[Center for Solar Energy and Hydrogen Research]] (''Zentrum für Sonnenenergie- und Wasserstoff- Forschung, ZSW'') in [[Ulm, Germany]].<ref name="Ulm">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat Robert A. Huggins |url=https://www.tf.uni-kiel.de/matwis/ionik/main/staff/guest_scientist/rhg/index.html |website=Lehrstuhl für Sensorik und Festkörper-Ionik |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref> where he remained until 1995.<ref name="ECS"/>
He was named Honorary Professor at both the University of Ulm (1994) and the University of Kiel (2000) in Germany.<ref name="ECS"/>

Huggins is the author, co-author or editor of over 400 publications including ''Advanced Batteries'' (2009) and ''Energy Storage: Fundamentals, Materials and Applications'' (2010, 1st; 2016, 2nd ed.)<ref name="Emeritus"/><ref name="ECS"/>
He holds at least 13 patents.<ref name="ECS"/>

* 2000, Honorary Professor, [[University of Kiel]]<ref name="ECS"/>
* 1994, Honorary Professor, [[University of Ulm]]<ref name="ECS"/>
* 1982, Battery Division Research Award, [[Electrochemical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Battery Division Research Award |url=https://www.electrochem.org/battery-division-research-award |website=The Electrochemical Society |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref>
* 1980, Case Centennial Scholar
* 1978,  Vincent Bendix Award, [[American Society for Engineering Education]]<ref name="ASEE">{{cite web |title=Past National Award Winners |url=https://www.asee.org/member-resources/awards/full-list-of-awards/awards-archive/past-national-award-winners-archive-2 |website=American Society for Engineering Education |access-date=29 September 2021}}</ref><ref name="Leslie"/>

* 1957,  Robert Lansing Hardy Award, [[American Institute of Mining, Metallurgical, and Petroleum Engineers]] (AIME)<ref name="TMS">{{cite web |title=AIME Robert Lansing Hardy Award |url=https://www.tms.org/portal/Professional_Development/Honors___Awards/AIME_Robert_Lansing_Hardy_Award.aspx |website=The Minerals, Metals & Materials Society (TMS) |access-date=30 September 2021}}</ref>

==Cold fusion==
While at Stanford, Huggins attempted to recreate the controversial work of [[Stanley Pons]] and [[Martin Fleischmann]] on the eventually discredited theory of [[cold fusion]].  At one point he reported success.<ref>{{cite news |last=Broad |first=William J. |title=Stanford Reports Success |date=April 19, 1989 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/04/19/us/stanford-reports-success.html}}</ref> Only  weeks later, such claims were rejected by a colleague.<ref>{{cite news |last=Browne |first=Malcolm W. |date=May 3, 1989 |title=Physicists Debunk Claim Of a New Kind of Fusion |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/05/03/us/physicists-debunk-claim-of-a-new-kind-of-fusion.html}}</ref>
